analysis:
The supplied units are base-side text from MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift, lines 1000-2053. The actual changes sit elsewhere: base ranges 825-836 and 1422, head ranges 789-799, 821-823, 1043-1044 and 1426-1428. The patch excerpt is truncated. It shows a reasoning-prefix computation (ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix and contentSeed) and a new stopStringScope argument (ReasoningStopScope.scope) added to the media submitTokenized call. The head-side lines for those ranges were not supplied, so I could not verify them. The changes at head 1043-1044 and 1426-1428 are also not visible in the base text provided.

What I reviewed in the base text: the text path's bridge submit, which fails loudly when there is no engine and fires releaseBox on errors. The cluster GLM image, GLM media, Qwen media and MiMo media prepare paths. makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream and makeEventStream, which handle cancellation, release and native consumer lease, and keep a terminal drain. The tokenize and applyTemplate helpers. In all of these, request cacheScope is passed through to the bridge as cacheSalt. cacheEnabled is false for the cluster and native media paths. The cluster image path also passes cacheEnabled false.

No security regression is visible, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated. The T-041 cache scoping (coordinator-authored cacheSalt) is passed through unchanged in the visible context. The new stopStringScope and reasoning-prefix logic affects output parsing and stop-string semantics, not trust boundaries, encryption or attestation. Reasoning withholding, T-008-style plaintext exposure and cancellation (T-010) were not shown to change.

Not verified: the head-side implementation of ReasoningStopScope, the stop-scope plumbing into the bridge, and the changes at head 1043-1044 and 1426-1428. A reviewer with the full head diff should confirm that stopStringScope cannot leak withheld reasoning, cannot bypass answer-stop filtering, and does not alter cache keying or cacheEnabled. These gaps are a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
